purpose: The contract the sandboxed content host is tested against. Every construct in hostile.epub appears here, and every entry here appears in hostile.epub; make-epub-fixtures.mjs fails to write either file if that stops being true.

fields.sectionId: Section (spine item id) that surfaces it.
fields.source: Zip entry the snippet literally appears in - the section document itself, or a stylesheet it pulls in.
fields.expectation: removed: must not survive into the rendered document. inert: may survive structurally but must not execute or navigate. preserved: MUST survive; removing it is a bug.
fields.probe: Global name a test asserts never appears. Unique per vector, so one failure cannot mask another.
fields.selector: Where present, a CSS selector for the element in the rendered document.
fields.snippet: The exact text in `source`, used to prove this list and the fixture agree.
fields.note: Anything about the vector that is not obvious from the markup.

sections.purpose: HTML script execution, navigation and embedding vectors, in head and body.
Inline SVG: a separate parsing context with its own script element, its own handler surface, xlink attributes, foreignObject and SMIL.
A spine item that is itself image/svg+xml, so the section document has no HTML wrapper at all.
Not well-formed XML on purpose: the text/html fallback path, plus the parser-confusion and encoding tricks that only exist there.
What a careless sanitizer breaks: zero-width page anchors, a self-closing non-void tag, an unresolvable drop-cap image, and ordinary structural markup.
Resource loading and the exfiltration channels: blob-rewritable references, an @import chain and cycle, and remote references that prove the CSP.
The only section declaring properties="scripted". It exists so the pair proves sanitization does not branch on the declaration.

unconditionalSanitization: Every attack vector except declared-scripted-script sits in a section whose manifest item does NOT declare properties="scripted". Section.scripted is an author declaration, not a detection, so a fixture that carried its attacks only behind the declaration could not prove that sanitization is unconditional. The one declared section carries the identical inline script for A/B comparison.

vectors.description: A <base> in the head that would re-point every relative reference at a remote origin.
A meta refresh that navigates the frame without script.
A <script src> pointing at a JavaScript file that really is in the archive and really is in the manifest, so resolve() would happily hand back bytes for it.
An inline <script> in the head.
An on* handler on <body> itself - the attribute a host that copies body attributes across would carry into its own document.
An onclick handler on a paragraph.

An on* handler written OnMouseOver with whitespace before the equals sign. XML preserves attribute case, so a sanitizer testing name.startsWith("on") misses it - and the name lowercases into a live handler the moment the tree is adopted into an HTML document.
A javascript: URL in an href. The anchor may survive; activating it must navigate nowhere and execute nothing.
The same scheme spelled with numeric character references, which the parser decodes before any attribute-value check sees it.
An onload handler on an image whose source really does resolve and really does load, so the handler fires with no user action if it survives.
An onerror handler on an image declared image/png whose bytes are not a PNG. It resolves, a blob: URL is built, decoding fails, and the handler fires - the classic that needs no user action.
A form whose action is a javascript: URL.
A form that would POST to a remote origin. The sandbox withholds allow-forms, but the element must not survive either.
A nested iframe pointing at a remote document.
An <object> with a remote data reference and a <param>.
An <embed> with a remote source.
A script inside a <template>. An HTML parse puts it in the template content fragment, which a sanitizer walking element.children never visits, and a serialize-and-reparse hands it straight back.
vectors.note: Inert until something clones the template content, so the assertion is that neither the element nor the script survives - an allowlist that has no entry for <template> gets this for free.

vectors.description: An onload handler on the <svg> root, which fires on its own.
A <script> in the SVG namespace, which an HTML-only element allowlist never sees.
A SMIL <set> that writes an event-handler attribute onto its parent after sanitization has already run over the attributes.
An onbegin handler on a SMIL <animate>, which fires by itself when the animation starts.
A <use> whose href is a data: SVG carrying a script.
The same vector spelled with the legacy xlink:href attribute, which a sanitizer that only knows the unprefixed name will leave in place.
A <foreignObject> that re-enters the XHTML namespace and carries a script there.
vectors.snippet: Foreign HTML inside SVG.

vectors.description: A SMIL <animate> that rewrites an anchor href to a javascript: URL after the fact.
An SVG anchor whose javascript: URL sits in xlink:href rather than href.
A script in a spine item that is itself an image/svg+xml document, so the whole section - not an embedded fragment - is parsed in the SVG namespace.
An onload handler on the root element of that SVG spine item.
The classic nested-tag construct aimed at regex sanitizers: stripping the inner <script> leaves a working one behind.
vectors.note: Inert by construction under a real HTML parser, which tokenizes this into an unknown element named scr<script rather than a script. It is here to pin that the host parses instead of pattern-matching; an allowlist must drop the unknown element regardless.

vectors.description: Unquoted attribute values, including an onerror on an image whose bytes are not a PNG. Illegal in XML, ordinary in HTML, and live once the fallback parser accepts it.

Mutation XSS: with scripting enabled the <noscript> body is raw text, so the img sits harmlessly inside a title attribute. Serialize that tree and parse it again in a context where noscript is parsed as markup, and the attribute boundary moves - the img escapes and its onerror is live. The exact shape a parse-sanitize-serialize-into-srcdoc pipeline has to survive.
A bare ampersand in text. The XHTML parse must fail and the HTML fallback must render the words, ampersand included.
vectors.snippet: The ledgers of Smith & Sons were kept in two hands

vectors.description: Content after an unclosed paragraph. MALFORMED_TAIL_SENTINEL must appear in the rendered text.
Two unclosed list items must render as two list items, not one.
A zero-width page anchor at block level. Sanitizing is not tidying: this is what fragment navigation, and later reading positions, resolve against.
The same construct mid-sentence, where an empty-inline cleanup pass is most tempting.
The publisher rule that makes those page anchors zero-width. It is why they are invisible and why a tidying pass is tempted to drop them.
An XHTML self-closing non-void tag. It must come out as an empty .

Everything after that anchor. An HTML parser ignores the slash, so a re-serialization that goes through raw markup lets the anchor swallow the remainder; SENTINEL_AFTER_SELF_CLOSING_ANCHOR and TAIL_SENTINEL_PRESERVE must both survive, and neither may end up inside the anchor.

A drop-cap image declared in the manifest but absent from the archive, so resolve() returns undefined. The alt text must be substituted back as a text node - dropping the image silently deletes the first letter of the chapter, which must read "The lamplighter".
Ordinary headings.
Inline <em> and <strong>.
vectors.snippet: kept two ledgers and never the same one twice

vectors.description: A well-formed list with three items.
A blockquote wrapping a paragraph.
vectors.snippet: We are paid to remember what the tide forgets.

vectors.description: A table with a head and a body.
A same-document fragment link. resolve() returns undefined for it by design, which must not be read as damage.
An image that resolves inside the archive; its src must become a blob: URL and load.
A linked stylesheet from inside the archive.
An @import of a second local stylesheet, written the way books write it - relative to the importing stylesheet, not to the section.
vectors.note: main.css lives in OEBPS/styles/ and the section in OEBPS/text/. Section.resolve() is section-relative, so the host must compose the reference in relative space (dirname of the link href, joined with the import target) before resolving. Resolving "second.css" straight from the section lands on OEBPS/text/second.css and returns undefined.

vectors.description: A url() inside an imported stylesheet pointing at an image that only exists relative to that stylesheet (OEBPS/styles/assets/plate.png).
vectors.note: The same relative-base trap as css-import-local, one level deeper: the base is second.css, which was itself reached through an @import.

vectors.description: An @font-face src pointing at a font inside the archive.
vectors.note: The .woff bytes are a stub, so the face will not render glyphs. What is assertable here is the rewrite and the resolution, not the typography.

vectors.description: A url() in an inline style attribute, whose base is the section itself.
cycle-a.css imports cycle-b.css. Following @import chains recursively must terminate rather than hang.
cycle-b.css imports cycle-a.css straight back, closing the cycle.
A linked stylesheet on a remote origin. Nothing may be fetched.
A remote tracking pixel. This one proves the CSP rather than the sanitizer: img-src blob: is what must stop it.
An @import of a remote stylesheet.
The CSS-only exfiltration channel: a background image on a remote origin with the payload in the query string.

An image declared in the manifest whose zip entry was never written; resolve() returns undefined. The element must degrade without throwing and the alt must come back as text, so the sentence reads "Declared in the manifest".

An image present in the archive but absent from the manifest. The manifest is the only statement of a media type, so resolve() returns undefined here too - a different failure class with the same graceful outcome, and the sentence must read "Undeclared in the manifest".

The control for the unconditional-sanitization criterion: the same inline script, in the one section whose manifest item declares properties="scripted". Its treatment must be identical to inline-script in the undeclared section.
